title: The Bhagavad Gita
examples: What is the Bhagavad Gita about?
Why did Arjuna not want to fight?

explain.say: The Bhagavad Gita, which means the Song of the Lord, is a conversation in about 700 verses between the warrior prince Arjuna and Krishna, who is driving his chariot. It sits inside the great Indian epic, the Mahabharata.

draw.text: A dialogue: Krishna teaches, Arjuna asks

explain.say: The scene is the battlefield of Kurukshetra in north India, where two branches of one royal family face each other before a great war. In the stories Krishna is linked with Mathura, where he was born, and Dwarka, his city by the sea.

draw.label: Places in the story of the Gita

draw.text: Kurukshetra: the field where the dialogue is set

explain.say: Arjuna looks across and sees his teachers, cousins and friends in the other army. Full of sorrow, he puts down his bow and refuses to fight, and the whole Gita is Krishna's answer to his doubt.

items: Arjuna sees loved ones in both armies
He lays down his bow in sorrow
Arjuna's doubt clears and he resolves to act

explain.say: Krishna teaches about dharma, your rightful duty, and says to act without clinging to the rewards. He also teaches that the true self, the atman, is never born and never dies.

draw.value: Your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits.
draw.label: Bhagavad Gita 2.47, a common rendering

draw.text: Atman: the true self, which does not die

explain.say: The Gita describes several paths, or yogas: karma yoga, the path of selfless action; jnana yoga, the path of knowledge; bhakti yoga, the path of loving devotion; and the path of meditation.

draw.text: Many readers see the paths as working together

explain.say: Hindu tradition places the dialogue at the start of the present age, thousands of years ago, while many historians date the text to the last centuries BCE. Today it is one of the most widely read sacred books in the world.

items: Tradition: start of the Kali Yuga, about 3100 BCE
Many scholars: composed about 5th to 2nd century BCE
About 800 CE: Shankara writes a famous commentary
1785: first English translation, by Charles Wilkins

draw.text: Traditional and scholarly dates are both shown

faq.q: What is the Bhagavad Gita about?
faq.a: The Gita is a conversation on a battlefield between Prince Arjuna, who does not want to fight his own relatives, and Krishna, his charioteer and guide. Krishna teaches him about duty, the eternal self, and paths to the divine through action, knowledge and devotion.
asks: What is the Gita about?
Tell me the story of the Bhagavad Gita
What happens in the Gita?

faq.a: Hindu tradition says the sage Vyasa composed it as part of the Mahabharata, with the words spoken by Krishna. Scholars think it was composed by poets whose names are not known, probably a few centuries before the common era.
asks: Who is the author of the Gita?
Who composed the Bhagavad Gita?
Did Vyasa write the Gita?

faq.q: How many chapters and verses are in the Bhagavad Gita?
faq.a: The Gita has 18 chapters and about 700 verses. Each chapter is called a yoga, like the yoga of action or the yoga of devotion.
asks: How many chapters does the Gita have?
How many shlokas are in the Gita?
How long is the Bhagavad Gita?

faq.q: Where is the Gita in the Mahabharata?
faq.a: The Gita is part of the Bhishma Parva, the sixth of the Mahabharata's 18 books. It comes just before the great battle of Kurukshetra begins.
asks: Is the Gita part of the Mahabharata?
Which book of the Mahabharata has the Gita?
How is the Gita connected to the Mahabharata?

faq.q: Who is Krishna in the Gita?
faq.a: In the story Krishna is Arjuna's cousin, friend and charioteer. Many Hindus revere Krishna as an avatar of the god Vishnu, so in the Gita his words are heard as divine teaching.
asks: Who is Lord Krishna?
Why is Krishna Arjuna's charioteer?
Is Krishna a god in the Gita?

faq.a: Arjuna is the third of the five Pandava brothers and the greatest archer of the epic. In the Gita he stands for anyone who faces a hard choice and asks what the right thing to do is.
asks: Who was Arjuna in the Gita?
Tell me about Arjuna
Which Pandava is Arjuna?

faq.q: Why did Arjuna not want to fight?
faq.a: Arjuna saw the revered elder Bhishma, his teacher Drona, cousins and friends in the opposing army. He felt that killing them would be wrong and would bring only grief, so he put down his bow.
asks: Why did Arjuna refuse to fight?
Why was Arjuna sad at Kurukshetra?
Why did Arjuna drop his bow?

faq.q: What does dharma mean in the Gita?
faq.a: Dharma means your rightful duty and the right way of living. In the Gita Krishna tells Arjuna that it is better to do your own duty, even imperfectly, than someone else's duty well.
asks: What is dharma?
What is duty in the Bhagavad Gita?
What does Krishna say about duty?

faq.a: Karma yoga is the path of selfless action: doing what is right because it is right, without being attached to the rewards. A famous verse, chapter 2 verse 47, says your right is to the action, not to its fruits.
asks: What does do your duty without expecting results mean?
What is the path of action in the Gita?
What is nishkama karma?

faq.q: What does the Gita say about the soul?
faq.a: The Gita teaches that the true self, the atman, is eternal: it is never born and never dies. It compares the self moving to a new body with a person putting on new clothes.
asks: Does the Gita say the soul never dies?
What is the atman in the Gita?
What happens after death in the Gita?

faq.q: What are the paths of yoga in the Gita?
faq.a: The Gita speaks of karma yoga, the path of selfless action; jnana yoga, the path of knowledge; and bhakti yoga, the path of loving devotion. It also teaches meditation, in chapter 6.
asks: What are the three paths in the Gita?
What is bhakti yoga?
What is jnana yoga?

faq.q: Is the Bhagavad Gita about war?
faq.a: It is set on a battlefield, but many readers, including Mahatma Gandhi, read the battle as a picture of the struggle inside each of us. Others read it as teaching about real duty, including a warrior's duty. Both readings are found in Hindu tradition.
asks: Does the Gita promote war?
Is the battle in the Gita symbolic?
Why is the Gita set on a battlefield?

faq.a: The conversation is told by Sanjaya, an adviser who is given the gift of seeing far away. He describes it to the blind king Dhritarashtra, the father of the Kauravas.
asks: Who tells the Gita to Dhritarashtra?
Who is Sanjaya?
How does the Gita begin?

faq.q: What language is the Bhagavad Gita written in?
faq.a: The Gita is written in Sanskrit verse, mostly in a four line metre called the shloka. It has been translated into most major languages; the first English translation, by Charles Wilkins, appeared in 1785.
asks: Is the Gita in Sanskrit?
When was the Gita translated into English?
What language did Krishna speak in the Gita?

facts: The Bhagavad Gita has 18 chapters and about 700 verses in Sanskrit.
The Gita is part of the Bhishma Parva, the sixth of the 18 books of the Mahabharata.
The Gita is set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, as a dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna.
Tradition attributes the Gita to the sage Vyasa; many scholars date it to roughly the 5th to 2nd century BCE.
The first English translation of the Gita, by Charles Wilkins, was published in 1785.

quiz.say: How many chapters does the Bhagavad Gita have?
quiz.show: How many chapters are in the Bhagavad Gita?
quiz.why: The Gita has 18 chapters and about 700 verses. Eighteen is a special number in the epic: the Mahabharata also has 18 books and its war lasts 18 days.

wrong.0: 12 is not right; the Gita has 18 chapters.
wrong.2: 24 is too many. You may be thinking of the 24,000 verses of the Ramayana.
wrong.3: 100 is far too many; the Gita is short, 18 chapters in all.

quiz.say: A student works hard on her science project and does her best, without worrying about whether she will win a prize. Which teaching of the Gita does this match?
quiz.show: Doing your best without clinging to the reward matches which teaching?

options.say: Karma yoga, the path of selfless action

quiz.why: Karma yoga means doing your duty well without being attached to its fruits, exactly what the student does.

wrong.1: The Gita says not to give up action; Krishna tells Arjuna to act, but without attachment.
wrong.2: Acting only for the prize is the opposite of karma yoga, which lets go of the reward.

quiz.say: Why do you think the Gita begins with Arjuna refusing to fight?
quiz.show: Why does the Gita begin with Arjuna's refusal?

options.show: It sets up the doubt the whole teaching answers
options.say: It sets up the doubt that the whole teaching answers

options.show: Krishna had told him to stop
options.say: Krishna had told him to stop

quiz.why: Arjuna's crisis about what is right gives Krishna the reason to teach. The rest of the Gita answers his questions about duty, the self and how to act.

wrong.1: Arjuna was not hurt; his sorrow was about fighting his own family and teachers.
wrong.2: It is the other way round: Krishna encourages Arjuna to do his duty.
wrong.3: The Gita takes place just before the battle begins.
